purpose: The DEVICE-LANE half of ci/open_reds.json. Same tool (`python ci/check_open_reds.py --register ci/open_reds_device.json`), same rules, different frame: every check here needs a Vulkan device and a built EP, so its colour cannot be observed on the host-free runner and must not be declared in the other file. ci/open_reds.json says so itself, twice, and ends both notes with 'it belongs in a device-lane register when one exists'. This is that register. It exists because `tests/ops` on main carried reds that no register had a name for -- I quoted `cargo test --lib` 540/0 after every merge as though it were the project's test result, and it is the Rust unit suite. The op suite is a different instrument measuring the thing users actually care about.
how_to_run: Set ONNXRUNTIME_VULKAN_EP_LIB to a FRESH release build (an unset variable makes tests/ops skip and several tools PASS having read nothing), then `python ci/check_open_reds.py --register ci/open_reds_device.json`. A run against a stale DLL is not a run: the proof ledger is include_str!'d, so a ledger change takes effect only at the next build.
not_wired_to_a_workflow: Stated rather than left to be discovered, because an unwired tool is invisible to ci/check_lane_inventory.py by construction -- that screen asks whether every workflow step has a Check, not whether every check has a step, and ci/check_verification_subjects.py arrived in ci/ with exactly this defect. This register is deliberately in NO workflow step today. The only GPU lane this repository has in CI is conformance.yml on ubuntu-22.04 + lavapipe, and neither entry can render a true colour there: criterion10 needs the Phi-3.5 artifact, which that lane does not fetch, so it would SKIP, exit 0, be observed green, and fail as stale_acceptance -- an acceptance revoked by an absence. The op-table Cast triple would be observable there, but splitting one register across two lanes so that half of it is ruled on is the shrinking-denominator defect this schema's `subjects` arm exists to catch. So it runs on the developer box that has the hardware and the model, which is where every reading in it was taken. Owner of the wiring question: Link. It closes when either a real-hardware lane exists or conformance.yml fetches the Phi-3.5 artifact; until then this note is the record that the omission is a decision.
how_to_add_an_entry: Identical to ci/open_reds.json -- an expect=red entry is a LEASE with an owner who can close it, a `closes_when` naming the observable event, and a `signature` that is the exact red accepted. Closing a red means setting expect=green and LEAVING IT RUNNING, never deleting the entry; `subjects` is append-only.

checks.reason: A DELIBERATE red with a real finding under it, red since 7d02f00 -- whose own commit title is 'criterion 10 compares 65 of 65, records the route, and STAYS DIVERGENT'. It has been an accepted red in someone's head for three sessions. The reading, not the exit code: 62 of 65 outputs are within tolerance; the three that are not are output 0 (logits) and outputs 63/64 (layer 31 key and value). Cross-run identity holds on all 65, argmax matches the CPU oracle exactly (30751), top-10 overlap is 10/10, and the ULP median over outputs is 1.0. Two things are behind the one red and they must not be merged: (a) an ACCURACY finding -- the per-layer median ULP curve rises monotonically 0 -> 4 through the 32 layers, and DESIGN.md 10.0.4 states that in ULPs a correct implementation's residual is expected FLAT, so a rise is a located finding; the recorded-before-measuring prediction (bench/results/criterion10-ulp-prediction.md, 'flat at 1-3 ULP') is exceeded at L31 by exactly 1 ULP. (b) a STATISTIC question -- output 0 fails an atol+rtol test (max_abs 0.0625 against 0.001 + 0.001*13.14) at a magnitude where 0.0625 is 8 fp16 ULP, and the same run's max_ulp_at_scale reads 8.0 while its raw max_ulp reads 255658.0 off 35 cancellation elements. Morpheus's degenerate-denominator ruling (8.9.22) is about exactly this shape: two numbers, never one. Neither half is mine to rule on -- I own FFI, ABI and the EP lifecycle -- and the honest outcome is a red with a written reason and two named owners, not a loosened tolerance.
checks.closes_when: EITHER Mouse accounts for the L31 step (a located kernel cause, or a re-derived ceiling that predicts 4 ULP at depth 32 BEFORE it is measured -- a ceiling raised after the fact predicts nothing) AND the outputs come inside the criterion; OR Morpheus rules on which statistic criterion 10 is decided by, at which point the criterion is restated and this entry is re-opened against the new one. checks.reason: THIS IS STILL THE ONE THING BLOCKING ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_DEVICE_MEMORY FROM SHIPPING ON. What has changed is that the fault is now REPRODUCIBLE ON DEMAND and four candidate causes are eliminated with a measurement each, so the next owner starts from a position instead of a guess. REPRODUCTION: rust/tools/device_loss_gate.py, resident lane, --steps 8 --seed-past 4096, DEVICE_MEMORY=1 BIND_OUTPUTS=1, arena off, uncapped. Arm A: rep0 LOST at Compute #6 after 1775 dispatches, rep1 and rep2 LOST at Compute #1 with 0 dispatches, rep3 and rep4 clean at 8/8 and 2840 dispatches. THREE IN FIVE - and that figure IS NOT COMPARABLE TO SWITCH'S 1/8, because --steps 8 is eight Compute() calls per observation against his two. The amplifier is --steps, not --reps: one observation costs ~145 s at --steps 2 and almost all of it is ORT session build over the 2.2 GB export. Do not average the two rates. EXTERNAL WITNESS, not produced by this project: Windows System log, provider nvlddmkm, Event Id 153, payload '\Device\UVMLiteController0x1 | Error occurred on GPUID: 100', at 2026-08-03 23:41:42 - the exact second of the stderr line in the signature record - and again at 2026-08-04 03:30:45, the exact second of my rep 0. Byte-identical payloads. NO Display Event 4101 in either window, so this is NOT a TDR and not a compute timeout; it is the driver's unified-memory paging path. Caveat that must travel with it: Id 153 is not rare on this box generally, so it corroborates the CLASS and does not on its own attribute an individual loss. ELIMINATED, each with its measurement: (1) THE ARENA, which was the handed-down prime suspect - with KV_ARENA=1 the EP REFUSES before any Compute ('an output was built as an alias of an input ... but is not bound to that input's device buffer'), because probe_kv_chain_phi35.py binds distinct `present` OrtValues; every run that has ever produced this fault had the arena OFF, including the signature run. (2) THIS EP'S OWN FOOTPRINT - alloc_high_water_bytes = 5518426760 in ten of ten repetitions, capped and uncapped, losing and clean; a constant cannot be the variable, and this also kills the ~7.1 GB arithmetic I predicted on, which double-counted the KV generations (the real peak is 5.52 GB on a 7959 MiB board). (3) BOARD OCCUPANCY - rust/examples/vram_occupant.rs holds and touches DEVICE_LOCAL memory from a foreign process; at 3584 MiB held, 3584 + 5262 = 8846 MiB does not fit in 7959 MiB, and the EP completed 8/8 Computes twice with 2840 dispatches, zero attach failures and zero losses. Four clean repetitions under co-tenancy; under the 3-in-5 rate measured here P(no loss in 4) = 0.026. (4) THE vkQueueSubmit CLASS - different call site, and Switch's queue_lock fix was in the tree for every repetition above. THE FIX I DID NOT SHIP, AND WHY IT MATTERS THAT I DIDN'T: I was about to default the EP's allocation ceiling to VkPhysicalDeviceMemoryBudgetPropertiesEXT::heapBudget instead of leaving budget_bytes() uncapped. I measured the instrument first. On this driver heapBudget is a CONSTANT 7191 MiB that does not move when a foreign process holds and touches 2560 MiB, and heapUsage counts this process only; nvidia-smi is worse, reporting memory.used = 0 MiB and [N/A] per compute app under the same load. The cap would never have bound, against a 5262 MiB peak - exactly the way the arm B --budget-mb 5600 cap never bound (alloc_high_water_bytes identical to the byte, alloc_device_attach_failures = 0). I would have shipped a change that cannot fire and quoted an inert arm as its evidence. Recorded because the shape recurs: two inert things agreeing is not corroboration. Answered on the way past, so nobody pays for it twice - VK_EXT_memory_budget does NOT need enabling on a VkDevice to be read; chaining onto vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties2 returns populated values with no device created, so caps.rs::required_device_extensions never needed touching. WHERE I WOULD LOOK NEXT: memory TYPE, not memory QUANTITY. The counters report alloc_unified_memory = 2 and the external witness names the unified-memory controller. Also recorded and explicitly NOT claimed as the cause: gqa_f16.comp reads history at t < past_len indexed against pc.past_stride with no t < past_stride guard (~lines 354, 413) while the write IS bounds-checked (~line 280) - not reachable in this configuration, but the right class of defect. WHAT IT STILL COSTS: unchanged. bench/results/runs_vs_does_not_run.json still rules ctx 4096 SPLIT and still refuses Niobe a citable claim there; ctx 8189 is unaffected and citable at 2/2. LANE IDENTITY RESOLVED 2026-08-04 (switch), because the reopened reason above eliminated the arena by showing the EP REFUSES under KV_ARENA=1, and that raised the question of what lane the signature run was actually in. Answer: DEVICE_MEMORY=1 with KV_ARENA OFF. It is NOT mis-attributed and it is NOT an arena fault. Two independent lines. (a) STRUCTURAL, and it is the decisive one: the signature record's failure is `vkWaitForFences failed: the Vulkan device was lost`, which is reached only AFTER a command buffer has been submitted. The alias sweep in vk/session.rs runs BEFORE any submit and bails the whole Compute. On Phi-3.5 `present` is declared symbolically (`total_sequence_length`), so `declared_present_len` is None and EVERY GQA node arenas when the flag is armed (ops/attention.rs, `let arena = ctx.kv_arena() && declared_present_len.is_none() && ...`) -- there is no partial arming. A run that reached a fence wait therefore had zero aliased outputs, therefore did not have the arena armed. The guard predates the loss: it landed in 0a91fda, 2026-08-03 10:14:55, and the loss is 2026-08-03 23:41:42. (b) MEASURED, at ctx 4096 on the merged build with both flags pinned explicitly in every arm: arm A (DEVICE_MEMORY=1, KV_ARENA=0) runs 710 dispatches with kv_cache_convention=GROWING, 4/4 clean; arm B (DEVICE_MEMORY=1, KV_ARENA=1) exits 1 at the alias refusal with 0 dispatches, confirming the refusal is total; arm C (KV_ARENA=1 on probe_kv_arena_phi35.py, which binds the SAME OrtValue as `past` input and `present` output, arena 4096 / past 4090) runs 710 dispatches with kv_cache_convention=SHARED, ARENA_TAKEN_AND_BIT_IDENTICAL, 0 losses. Arm C is the case the brief called `a probe that binds correctly`: the arena executes at this context and did not lose the device in this observation. One observation is not a rate and is not offered as one -- the attribution rests on (a). Artifacts: bench/results/lane-identity-arm{A-arena0,B-arena1,C-arena4096}.json and lane-identity-armA-screened-r{1,2,3}.json, each carrying `env_pinned` and `kv_cache_convention` in the record, which the signature record did not. WHAT THIS COSTS THE SCORING, and it is not nothing. The four-gate scoring applied one discriminator, written down before any run: A GATE BLOCKS THE FLIP ONLY IF ITS FAILURE SEPARATES THE LANES. That discriminator was never actually applied to this gate, and when applied it does not hold -- not because the armed lane is clean, but because THE UNARMED LANE CANNOT BE OBSERVED AT ctx 4096. Measured 2026-08-04, deterministic, 3 of 3: the DEVICE_MEMORY=0 lane at seed_past 4096 fails inside ORT with `gpu-allocator failed to allocate 14155776 bytes for 'ep_in_427': Out of memory`, ORT silently re-executes all 355 nodes on the CPU EP, and the worker exits 0 with no exception and dispatches_executed = 0. So at this context there is no OFF lane to compare against: the flag cannot be shown to cause the loss, because the only lane that reaches a dispatch is the armed one. Recorded as a separate subject, device_memory_ctx4096_shipping_lane_cannot_run. This entry therefore keeps its id (subjects is append-only) but its CORRECTED NAME is: an UNSEPARATED device loss at ctx 4096, reachable only on the device-resident lane because it is the only lane that runs there. It is a real fault and Tank's closes_when stands unchanged. || 2026-08-04, SWITCH, THE COMPARISON NOW EXISTS AND HERE IS WHAT IT SAYS. The prefix alias made the shipping lane executable at ctx 4096, so the fault can be sought in BOTH lanes for the first time. 20 repetitions, --steps 8 --seed-past 4096, lanes INTERLEAVED by repetition index so lane assignment is orthogonal to time order, one binary, DEVICE_MEMORY the only pinned difference, 20/20 non-vacuous, 157 Compute() calls observed. RESULT: 1 loss, resident lane, at vkWaitForFences -- Tank's class exactly -- versus 0 in 10 shipping repetitions and 80 shipping Compute() calls. THE VERDICT IS SEPARATES_UNDERPOWERED, NOT SEPARATES, and the tool now computes that downgrade itself: if the shipping lane's true rate equalled the resident lane's OBSERVED 1/10, it would still show zero in 10 runs at probability 0.349. An absence at that power is not a difference. WORSE FOR ATTRIBUTION: the one loss landed at repetition 0 -- the first, coldest run of the session -- which is the single worst position for distinguishing lane from time order, and is precisely the confound the interleaving was built to remove. CORRECTNESS IS NOT AT ISSUE: 9 resident and 10 shipping repetitions produced BIT-IDENTICAL logits, one digest across both lanes (bench/results/lane_logits_identity-ctx4096.json). So this red survives its own discriminator only in the weak sense that the fault has not yet been seen with the flag off, and the honest next step is exposure in the SHIPPING lane, not more repetitions of the resident one. Evidence: bench/results/device_loss_gate-BOTHLANES.json.

checks.reason: A red that ARGUES FOR THE FLIP rather than against it, which is why it is declared instead of being left as a paragraph. Gate 3 was 'concurrent sessions', and I pre-registered the prediction that it would be the sole blocker -- that the device-resident lane would be the one that broke when two sessions overlapped. bench/results/device-memory-flip-gates-prediction.md has that in writing, before the run. The measurement reversed it. Over 6 rounds of two overlapping Phi-3.5 sessions (overlap proven by max_concurrent_depth=2, not assumed): res_threads is 0/6 dirty, 1560/1560 outputs bit-identical to the serial lane, 8520 dispatches equal to serial. ship_threads is 6/6 dirty, 780/1560 outputs mismatched on the register run and 130/260 on the first 6-round run -- the mismatch COUNT is not stable across runs and must not be quoted as if it were; what reproduces is 6/6 dirty rounds and 0 EP dispatches. The lane EXITS 0 WITH NO EXCEPTION because ORT swallows the EP Compute failure and silently rebuilds on CPU. The default configuration returns wrong-provider answers under concurrency and says nothing. The cause is in the text, not inferred: `alloc_device failed for input buffer`. The shipping path allocates a transient per-Compute input device buffer, so two overlapping Computes double the peak on an 8 GB card; the resident path's inputs are already resident, so it allocates strictly less and survives. THE DISCRIMINATOR MATTERS AND I ALMOST SKIPPED IT: the first version of this probe had three lanes and no ship_threads. In that version res_threads was the lane that raised, and I was one step from filing 'device memory breaks under concurrency' as a blocker. A failure in the armed lane is only attributable to the flag if the unarmed lane is run too. Adding the fourth lane inverted the finding completely.
checks.closes_when: The shipping lane stops silently producing CPU results under concurrent sessions -- either the transient per-Compute input allocation is removed or bounded so two overlapping Computes fit, or the EP refuses loudly instead of letting ORT fall back without a word. Note that flipping DEVICE_MEMORY on by default would ALSO close it, by making the resident path the default, and that is the point of filing it here: it is evidence in the flip's favour that would otherwise live in a paragraph nobody runs.
checks.signature_note: A literal substring of the probe's own summary line, not prose. My first attempt described the red in a sentence and check_open_reds.py returned FAIL(condition=signature_changed) against it -- correctly, twice in one session, which is how I learned the signature is matched as a substring. This string pins three things at once: the lane (ship_threads), that the overlap actually happened (depth=2 -- a lane that never overlapped cannot have failed under concurrency), and the rate (6/6, not one bad round). Note it also pins exit=0, which is the whole finding: the lane FAILS and EXITS CLEAN.

checks.reason: Gate 2 of the four, CLOSED by running it rather than by reasoning about it, and declared green so that it is RUN. It was #[ignore]d, which on this project means invisible: nobody had observed its colour, and 'we think the MIXED frame is handled' was a belief with no instrument under it. Run with ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_DEVICE_MEMORY=1 it passes and it prints the thing worth knowing: device_index 0 declares frame SPLIT-DEVICE with 1 allocator declared, then device_index 1 moves the frame to MIXED with 2 declared. It changes what may be REPORTED, never a byte of output. It does not block the flip. It stays #[ignore]d in the default suite because it needs two physical devices and would fail on a one-device box for a reason that has nothing to do with the code; this entry is how it gets run anyway, on the box that has the hardware. Un-ignoring it would trade an invisible test for a falsely red one.

checks.reason: Gate 4 of the four, CLOSED, and the artifact behind the one performance claim this project can make without a clock. At context 8189 on the RTX 4060 the growing-KV configuration's worker exits 1 and produces no counters at all, while the arena configuration completes 355 dispatches per step at an allocation high-water of 5,512,528,520 B and a KV slope of 32,064 B per past token. Reproduced live against the merged build today, digit-for-digit against a record from a previous session: 2 of 2 within-record pairs agree. 'Runs' versus 'does not run' is not a ratio, so it cannot be inflated by choosing an arm, and it does not need a timer -- which matters this round because the project has never been timed and Niobe's paired-alternation measurement is the first attempt. THE TOOL EXISTS SO THE CLAIM IS DERIVED RATHER THAN TYPED. Every number in bench/results/runs_vs_does_not_run.json is read out of a named record at build time and carried with that record's sha256; there are no literals in it. It refuses three things that have each cost this project a session: it never pairs lanes from two different probe invocations, it never reads exit code 0 as evidence the EP ran (a lane can exit 0 having executed ZERO dispatches because ORT silently rebuilt on CPU -- that gets its own class, COMPLETED_WITHOUT_EP, and is not a fast run), and a lane with no counters file classifies as DID_NOT_COMPLETE rather than being skipped into silence. MOST IMPORTANTLY IT AGGREGATES BY DIRECTION AND SO IT CAN REFUSE ME. At ctx 4096 it reads SPLIT -- 4 pairs favour device-resident, 1 favours shipping, that 1 being the device loss registered above -- and it marks that context NOT citable, even though the majority runs my way and even though the brief for this round asserted the ctx 4096 claim as settled. A tool that only ever confirms the person who wrote it is not an instrument.

checks.reason: HISTORICAL: the shipping lane could not run Phi-3.5 at ctx 4096 at all, and it said so only on stderr -- ORT re-executed the fused subgraph on the CPU EP, get_providers() still listed VulkanExecutionProvider, and the process EXITED 0. The cause was arithmetic, not architecture: the EP allocated a full `past` buffer per Compute, uploaded into it, had the shader copy it into `present`'s prefix, and threw it away. The prefix alias stages `past`'s bytes straight into `present` and never allocates `past`. NOTE THE BOUNDARY: this entry was named after the string it was found by (`alloc_device failed` at 4096); the lane actually died at 3072, and the 6144/8192 figures quoted elsewhere in this project were never the shipping lane's. The check is now LIVE rather than a scan of a frozen artifact, because an entry whose evidence is a file on disk can only ever report the day it was written.

It STAYS RUNNING as a green, per this register's own rule, and it goes red the day the shipping lane stops executing: the gate returns REFUSE(2) rather than PASS when a requested lane produces no non-vacuous observation, which is the exact shape of the failure this entry was opened for -- 355 nodes claimed, 0 dispatches, exit 0.

checks.reason: DECLARED GREEN SO IT IS RUN, because for one merge it was neither green nor red -- it was unobserved. ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_KV_PREFIX_ALIAS ships ON. With ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_DEVICE_MEMORY=1 it killed the process with an ACCESS VIOLATION (exit 3221225477 = 0xC0000005) on the FIRST Compute: 0 dispatches, no Vulkan error, no log line, no exception. Deterministic, 4 of 4 (3 at seed_past 4096, 1 at 512); the same binary with KV_PREFIX_ALIAS=0 completed 710 dispatches. MECHANISM: the alias stages the aliased input's HOST bytes, and an input ORT placed in this EP's device memory has none -- its pointer is a reserved, inaccessible address by design (vk/session.rs Step 1b's own comment). Step 1b converts such a pointer to readable bytes only for inputs Step 1a did NOT bind; the prefix staging loop read it anyway. The guard did its job and faulted rather than reading a neighbouring tensor. Nobody asked it the question. FIX: Step 1a is hoisted above the translate pre-pass, ShapeOnlyRecorder carries a per-Compute `growing_alias_available`, and kv_growing_alias() is now flag AND capability -- the alias is declined for the whole island whenever any plan input is device-bound. Nothing is lost: when `past` is already a device buffer the caller owns there is no allocation to save, and the shader's own copy_leader does the past->present copy on the device. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITSELF: the crash was invisible only because the lane it breaks is behind a flag that is also off by default. TWO DEFAULTS WERE LOAD-BEARING FOR EACH OTHER, and flipping DEVICE_MEMORY on without this fix would have turned a flag nobody sets into an access violation for every user at every context length.
